messages:
lee: Heads up — seeing a spike of 502/503s from edge-proxy in eu-west2 since ~08:45 UTC. Svc appears healthy but backend connections are being reset. Anyone touching SG/NACLs overnight?

maria: I updated a couple security groups for the image-puller nodes to tighten ranges (reduced ephemeral ports). Could that be it? :grimacing:

jon: Wasn't me. What range did you set them to?

maria: Set node SG egress ephemeral to 32768-61000 -> but I also added a NACL on the subnet to 32768-35000 (trying to limit noisy hosts).

lee: That seems like a partial overlap. Edge-proxy and ALB healthchecks rely on ephemeral source ports for backend connections. If NACL cuts a subset, we can get asymmetric drops.

sam: Ops-bot shows a canary deploy at 08:40 but latency started climbing ~08:44. Could be coincident. ops-bot: canary-deploy-edge-proxy-2026-03-18 completed :white_check_mark:

lee: Grabbed tcpdump on one edge node. Snippet:```
10:45:12.123 IP 10.10.5.22.57823 > 10.20.3.11.8080: Flags [S], seq 12345
10:45:12.129 IP 10.20.3.11.8080 > 10.10.5.22.57823: RST, seq 1
```

jon: RST from backend indicates packet reached backend then backend reset, or path back blocked. Can you `traceroute` from the ALB to backend?

lee: traceroute shows leaf hops fine. I also ran `kubectl describe svc edge-proxy -n prod` — endpoints healthy. No pod restarts.

maria: I think the NACL deny rule for 35001-61000 is missing; I accidentally only allowed 32768-35000 and forgot to allow the rest for the backend group. Means some source ports are allowed and others dropped -> fragmenting connection pool.

sam: That explains inconsistent 502s. ALB uses high source ports when proxying. If NACL denies return path for those, backends RST or ALB gives 502.

lee: Quick mitigation — can someone add an allow outbound on the subnet NACL for ephemeral 32768-65535 (temporary) and we’ll tighten after root cause verified?

maria: On it. Doing `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 110 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow --egress true --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=65535` (pseudo). Applying now.

(1 minute later)

maria: Patch applied. Monitoring.

lee: Errors dropped to baseline within 90s after change. Good.

jon: Follow-up action items: 1) revert SG tightening until we have a policy doc for ephemeral port handling 2) add test in infra-e2e that simulates ALB->pod return path with NACLs 3) capture exact rules we applied and tag who changed them.

sam: I'll file a short incident note in postmortems with root cause = partial ephemeral port range allow leading to asymmetric NACL behavior; include rules and timestamps.

maria: Sorry about the slip — lesson learned. Will make change request and coordinate with eng-infra before making NACL changes. :raised_hands:

lee: Thanks team. Closing the thread once postmortem links up.

ops-bot: incident-created: INC-20260318-031 — assigned to sam for documentation.
